'''Ashvin Vishwanath''' (born January 9, 1973) is an Indian-American [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] known for important contributions to [[condensed matter physics]]. He is a professor of physics at [[Harvard University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.physics.harvard.edu/people/facpages/vishwanath|title=Faculty: ASHVIN VISHWANATH {{!}} Harvard University Department of Physics|website=www.physics.harvard.edu|access-date=2017-10-17}}</ref>

Vishwanath was elected as a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=New Members|url=https://www.amacad.org/new-members-2021|access-date=2021-04-24|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|language=en}}</ref>

==Education and career==

Vishwanath holds an undergraduate degree from  [[IIT Kanpur|Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur]], completed in 1996. He received his Ph.D. in physics from [[Princeton University]] in 2001, after completing a doctoral dissertation, titled "Vortices, [[quasiparticle]]s and unconventional [[superconductivity]]", under the supervision of [[Duncan Haldane|F. Duncan Haldane]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Vishwanath|first=Ashvin|url=https://catalog.princeton.edu/catalog/3424707|title=Vortices, quasiparticles and unconventional superconductivity|date=2001|language=English}}</ref> Between 2001 and 2004 he was a Pappalardo fellow at [[MIT]], where his collaborators included [[Todadri Senthil|T. Senthil]] and [[Subir Sachdev]]. He joined the physics faculty at [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 2004 and moved to [[Harvard University]] in 2016.<ref name=":0" /> He held a Distinguished Visiting Research Chair at the [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]] from 2012 to 2015 and was awarded the [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] in materials science in 2014. He is one of the recipients of the 2016 [[EPS Europhysics Prize]] in condensed matter physics for theoretical studies on magnetic skyrmion phases in MnSi, a new phase of matter.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.eps.org/members/group_content_view.asp?group=85187&id=554142|title=CMD Europhysics Prize - European Physical Society (EPS)|author=European Physical Society|website=www.eps.org|access-date=2017-10-18}}</ref> He is one of the recipients of the 2024 [[Oliver E. Buckley Prize]] for groundbreaking theoretical and experimental studies on the collective electronic properties of materials that reflect topological aspects of their band structure.<ref>{{cite web |title = 2024 Oliver E. Buckley Condensed Matter Physics Prize Recipient |url = https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Vishwanath&first_nm=Ashvin&year=2024 | website = American Physical Society | access-date = 2023-10-26}}</ref> He is also a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sites.google.com/site/ashvinvish/Home|title=Vishwanath Group Homepage|website=sites.google.com|access-date=2017-10-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160826214646/https://sites.google.com/site/ashvinvish/Home|archive-date=2016-08-26|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Research ==
Vishwanath has made important contributions to several areas in condensed matter physics. In particular, his most important contributions have been in deconfined quantum criticality (with [[T. Senthil]], [[Matthew P. A. Fisher]], [[Subir Sachdev]] and [[Leon Balents]]), Dirac and [[Weyl semimetal]]s, iron-based [[High-temperature superconductivity|high-temperature superconductors]], magnetic skyrmion phases, and [[topological insulator]]s where, in particular and more recently, he has explored several aspects and field theories of symmetry protected topological phases and Floquet topological phases. He has also done important works on quantum magnetic systems and quantum entanglement properties of spin liquids and related topological orders.
